Short answer: yes. Long answer, I don't know what people expect from a nearly 70-year-old movie with a black guy as one of the main characters. Uncle Remus (a former slave) tells stories in the stereotypical poor/slave English and there are some songs. Plenty of offensive content (like tar babies). It also has one of the catchiest songs (zip a dee doo dah). As a kid, I enjoyed the film very much. I don't defend it but rather accept it for what it is. Same with movies like White Christmas where people dance around in black face. Not acceptable at all by today's standards but to pretend movies like those didn't exist is worse (in my opinion).

I don't know. I heard that the stories used in Song of the South were created by black slaves. It would be a hard movie to make, but I wouldn't think that alone would make it racist. I'd get a copy and decide for myself, but I hear it's hard to find and boring as sin.

I bought my copy from Canada on ebay. I watch it from time to time. It did a lot of things - like apply morals to the stories, show a black person as a main character, and entertained while doing it. The stories are gathered from a published collection but I thought they were compiled by a white author trying to keep black oral traditions alive. How close the movie comes the the original stories or whether liberties were taken by the author, well, I have no idea. I rather liked Uncle Remus (in the movie) since it seemed he genuinely cared about the little runaway boy. It's just a kid's movie wherein a black plantation worker befriends a boy struggling with his parents separation (although I don't think it was marital, just physical). Even if it was available on DVD, I doubt most people would be interested enough to make it to the end of the film. Although the animation/live-film was cutting edge at the time, it just looks silly now. It's the kind of film that would show up on netflix for novelty if not for the criticism surrounding it.
